## Overview

This model compares phonetic spelling (`spphon`) over one intervention-aligned window per child. The immediate arm uses t1 to t3; the wait-list arm uses t2 to t4. The model estimates the endpoint score given the onset score, age at onset and Block Design score. Each child contributes one row, so there is no child random intercept.

**Off-floor outcome.** Phonetic spelling is **heavily floored**, so this uses the suite floor rule: `likelihood="bernoulli_offfloor"` — a **Bernoulli on the off-floor indicator** (aligned post $> 0$), with no `kappa`; the linear predictor is the log-odds of being off the floor at the endpoint and the cohort marginal collapses to an **off-floor risk difference**. The own-baseline term is the **binary off-floor-at-onset indicator** (`gamma_own_offfloor` ~ Normal(0, 1)), not the graded onset logit: with most children at the onset floor the graded logit is a near-degenerate spike and the graded Normal(1, 0.25) tracking prior implied an unintended, strongly pessimistic intercept for at-floor children (#391 finding 2, adopted here by the 2026-08-21 aligned review).

**The cohort contrast is an association.** The windows differ in age at onset, calendar timing and elapsed time. The immediate window averages 15.5 months and the wait-list window 14.2 months. Alignment does not equalise elapsed time or sessions received. Use the ITT suite for the randomised assignment contrast. Session dose enters only the separate sensitivity variant. See [the assessment-interval decision](../../../notes/202609212100-assessment-interval-lengths.md).

## Model

$$
(P_{\text{post(aligned)}} > 0) \sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(\operatorname{expit}(\eta)),\quad
\eta = \alpha + \beta_{\text{cohort}}\,\text{immediate}
  + \gamma_{\text{own-offfloor}}\,[P_{\text{onset}} > 0]
  + \gamma_A A_{\text{onset,std}} + \gamma_{\text{ability}}z(\text{blocks}).
$$

One row per child; no `kappa` under the off-floor Bernoulli. Priors follow the shared template in `priors.py`.
